question: Why does the author say that sincere readers will recognize the authority of this exposition without need for praise?
premises: The supreme lord composed this scripture under the name Jñānacandra.
The author has explained it clearly and profoundly to establish the authority of his own tradition.
For minds that have entered this teaching, the greatness of its authority shines forth, exalted by universal nonduality.
inference: Therefore sincere readers will recognize its truth on their own, making self-praise unnecessary.
plain_english: In this scripture composed by the Supreme Lord under the name Jñānacandra, I have explained this clear yet profound statement, following the method of establishing the authority of our own tradition and also through various relevant contexts. For those whose minds have entered into it, the greatness of its authority, exalted by universal nonduality, shines forth; sincere-hearted people will know this for themselves, so what need is there for praise?
